prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports and pull requests as a burden, based on the provided search results.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "We need to reduce the amount of sand in the machine. We must do something to drastically reduce the temptation for users to submit low quality reports. Be it with AI or without AI." | CLAIM: The curl project views low-quality, AI-generated reports as a burden that clogs up their workflow and requires intervention.
SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "The curl security team consists of seven team members... Every report thus engages 3-4 persons. Perhaps for 30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each." | CLAIM: AI slop vulnerability reports are a significant burden because they consume massive amounts of the maintainers' limited time to triage.
SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: Dealing with AI-generated reports takes an emotional toll on maintainers.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: The volume of invalid AI-generated security reports is so high and time-consuming to triage that it acts as a DDoS attack on the project.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "He went on to say that the project has never received a single valid bug report that was generated using AI, and their rate is increasing." | CLAIM: All AI-generated vulnerability reports submitted to curl have been invalid, yet their increasing volume continues to waste maintainer time.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports" | CLAIM: Python's Seth Larson highlighted that low-quality AI security reports cause stress, frustration, and contributor burnout.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious. Even if this is not their intent, the outcome is maintainers that are burnt out and more averse to legitimate security work." | CLAIM: Seth Larson of Python considers low-quality AI security reports effectively malicious due to the burnout they cause among maintainers.
SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time" | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg declared that curl is being DDoSed by AI-generated reports and views them as a massive waste of unpaid maintainer time.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "is not only the volume goes up, the quality goes down. So we spend more time than ever to get less out of it than ever." | CLAIM: AI-generated reports force maintainers to spend more time reviewing for worse results.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly. They don’t really understand it, they haven’t really verified it." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg views the submission of unverified, AI-generated reports as an abuse of maintainers' time because reporters put in zero effort while the maintainers are forced to do hours of work.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "Previously, I mean two years ago, every such report, it actually meant that the reporter, if it had some kind of substance, it meant that the reporter actually spent some time thinking, testing, verifying. They actually invested something and then passed it on. And that made it, it was a built-in sort of balance to the whole thing. That balance is off now." | CLAIM: AI has destroyed the built-in balance of bug reporting, where reporters previously had to invest their own time and effort before dumping work onto maintainers.
SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bug-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We are just a small single open source project with a small number of active maintainers... We need to make moves to ensure our survival and intact mental health." | CLAIM: The burden of AI slop reports became so heavy that the curl project entirely scrapped its bug bounty program to protect the mental health and survival of its maintainers.
SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bug-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We will ban you and ridicule you in public if you waste our time on crap reports." | CLAIM: The curl project has resorted to public ridicule and bans for reporters who submit AI slop to shield maintainers from the burden.
SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bug-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "AI slop is overwhelming maintainers *today* and it won’t stop at curl but only starts there" | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg warned that AI slop is currently overwhelming open source maintainers and will spread beyond curl as a broader industry burden.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: Seth Larson (Python) stated that AI slop reports are a burden because they appear legitimate and require expensive, time-consuming investigation by trained maintainers to debunk.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Specific documented quotes from maintainers of projects *other* than curl and Python (such as FFmpeg) explicitly naming AI-generated reports as a burden in their own words, beyond a brief mention by Stenberg that FFmpeg gets overloaded with reports from tech giants.
